title: The Cake on the Lake
checkpoint: Year 1 Autumn 2, week 2 — School readiness — Phase 5: new sounds a-e, are
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 5 book for the split spelling 'a-e'. The a and the e work as a team with a letter sitting in between them — c-a-k-e. Draw a little bridge over the top from the a to the e and your child will start spotting it everywhere.

pages.text: Nell had made a cake. It was not a big cake, but it had her name on it.
pages.illustration: Nell the bee beside a small lopsided honey-coloured cake on a leaf plate, her name spelled out in seeds on the top. She is beaming. Warm gold light.

pages.text: She had to take it to the lake. Moss came to help, but he was not fast.
pages.illustration: Nell hovering with the leaf plate; Moss plodding beside her at a fraction of the speed, tongue out with effort. A long path stretching ahead of them. Comic pacing.

pages.text: The path by the lake was wet. Moss did not make it past the mud.
pages.illustration: Moss stuck to his middle in thick brown mud, spikes flat with dismay, holding the cake plate high and clean above his head. Reeds and reflections all round.

pages.text: Ned came. He said the cake was his to take — and it went right into the lake.
pages.illustration: The instant of disaster: Ned reaching for the plate, one foot slipping, the cake sailing off in a graceful arc towards the water. Everyone caught mid-horror. Strong diagonal.

pages.text: The cake did not sink. It sat on the lake like a little raft.
pages.illustration: Calm wide shot of the lake surface with the small cake floating serenely in the middle, perfectly upright, seeds still spelling Nell's name. Still water, soft reflections. Absurd and lovely.

pages.text: A duck swam up. Ned made a noise at him and said the cake was not for him.
pages.illustration: Another duck paddling hopefully towards the floating cake; Ned in the water between it and the cake, wings spread wide and beak set. Territorial and hilarious.

pages.text: So they ate the cake on the lake, on a flat rock, and no one made a fuss at all.
pages.illustration: The three of them on a flat wet rock in the shallows with the rescued cake between them, damp and happy, sharing it in crumbs. Late afternoon light on the water.
